intro.author: Not named. It continues 1 Samuel, which was one book with it in Hebrew. Jewish tradition credits the prophets Gad and Nathan with completing the account (compare 1 Chronicles 29:29); it likely drew on court records and eyewitness memories.
intro.written: Uncertain; traditionally soon after David's reign (around 970 BC), while many scholars date its final form to after the kingdom divided or later
intro.audience: Israel, looking back on the reign of its model king and the promise God made to his family
intro.setting: The book covers David's forty-year reign, traditionally about 1010–970 BC (5:4). He rules Judah from Hebron for seven and a half years, then all Israel from Jerusalem, which he captures from the Jebusites. After his sin with Bathsheba, the story turns to violence and rebellion within his own family.
intro.purpose: To show God establishing David's throne and promising him a lasting dynasty, while telling honestly how the king's sin brought heavy consequences.
intro.bigIdea: God keeps his promise to David even when David fails, yet sin still bears bitter fruit.

outline.title: The kingdom established and the promise given
Closing records, songs and a plague
